public_rationale: The deadline has passed. Before even the earlier June anniversary, mathematicians verified an AI-generated disproof of the unit-distance conjecture and assessed it as an exceptional research contribution. This seriously challenges Marcus's dismissal. However, outstanding research output and the broader capability of a world-class mathematician are not interchangeable, a distinction Gowers explicitly makes. A definite verdict would turn on a threshold Marcus did not specify.
limitations: Under a narrower reading requiring a world-class research result, the May disproof would contradict the forecast.
The evidence does not justify treating failure to establish broader capability as proof that it was absent.
Some human involvement refined the exposition of the unit-distance proof; the companion paper distinguishes that from its initial mathematical generation.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There will not be AI-based world-class mathematicians within a year (by about July 2026).

statement.excerpt: Eric Schmidt’s recent prediction (made before IMO 2025), that there will be AI-based “world-class mathematicians” within a year, is pure fantasy.
statement.document_title: DeepMind and OpenAI achieve IMO Gold. What does it all mean?

our_interpretation: Read as a firm negative forecast about AI reaching world-class research-mathematician capability within the referenced year.
The ordinary research-context reading requires independently validated original mathematics and expert assessment that the system can work at that level. An olympiad result alone is insufficient.
Schmidt's episode was recorded on June 5, 2025 and published on July 17, 2025. July 17, 2026 is the latest anniversary of those two anchors; the earlier anniversary is June 5, 2026.
A major autonomous research result is substantial counterevidence, but equating one result with the broader capability of a world-class mathematician is an additional interpretation.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence covering the deadline establishes that available AI systems had not attained world-class mathematical research capability, rather than merely failing to find a qualifying example in a search.
criteria.contradiction_condition: By the deadline, an AI system demonstrates independently validated original research and receives sufficiently clear expert assessment of world-class research capability.

evidence.explanation: The surrounding passage contains Schmidt's one-year prediction about AI mathematicians. The episode description supplies the June recording and July publication dates used to interpret the deadline.

evidence.locator: Section 5, W T Gowers; proof and provenance in Section 1
evidence.publisher: arXiv; Noga Alon and eight other mathematicians
evidence.explanation: The authors verify an AI-generated unit-distance disproof, and Gowers judges it worthy of the Annals of Mathematics. This is substantial counterevidence before either deadline, although Gowers expressly distinguishes problem solving from other mathematical activities.

evidence.locator: Section 1, item A, Reliable autonomous research
evidence.explanation: Aletheia supplies additional evidence of autonomous research before the deadline. The authors also state that their autonomous results are not claimed as major mathematical advances, so this does not independently settle the world-class threshold.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Independent assessments of systems demonstrated by the deadline that establish their research capability against an explicit, defensible world-class standard, including the extent of human assistance.
